pr_title: fix(test runner): more friendly test duration
pr_body:
Reported test duration now does not include time spent in `beforeAll`, `afterAll` and fixtures that have a separate timeout.
This is to avoid different reported test execution time, depending on the test execution order.

Fixes #15338.

issue_context.title: [BUG] Worker-scope fixture setup skewing test duration
issue_context.body:
Hi! 👋 

**Context:**
- Playwright Version: 1.22.2
- Operating System: macOS 12.1 Monterey
- Node.js version: v18.4.0
- Browser: Chrome
- Extra: I doubt the environment plays a role

**Describe the bug**
The duration of any worker-scoped fixture setup is attributed to the first test that the worker runs afterwards.
i.e. if there's a worker-scoped fixture that takes 20s to setup, and the worker runs 3 tests that each take 5 seconds, the report will say that:
1. test 1 (25s) -> so: counting fixture setup.
2. test 2 (5s)
3. test 3 (5s)

This:
a) greatly skews the metrics for tests duration
b) is non-deterministic, as the fixture setup is not done consistently previous to the same test across runs (if e.g. there's a test failure and the worker restarts)

IMO, duration of worker-scoped fixtures setup should be reported (still, but) completely outside of individual test duration, that'd be my user expectation.
comments: Yes, I've been trying to understand this myself. This doesn't seem to be in line with the documented behaviour here: https://playwright.dev/docs/test-timeouts#fixture-timeout but I've been trying to figure out if I'm just configuring this wrong.

It looks to me as though https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/15117 which has been merged, but is awaiting a tagged release, might fix this issue. I haven't been able to test to confirm though.
There's been some work on this front, cc'ing Dmitry for details.

This is explained in [test timeout](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-timeouts#test-timeout) section - all fixtures are included in the test time. However, you can opt-out of this behavior for any fixture by setting a separate `timeout` for it, as explained in [this section](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-timeouts#fixture-timeout). Let me know whether that works for you.

...and tested with your comment to see if I misunderstood, so changed to:
```ts
...
    { scope: "worker", timeout: 21000 },
...
```
...to see if that would 'isolate' the _duration_ as well as the timeout, but the output was the exact same, so my issue is, I believe, valid

I've also experienced what @raulparada has experienced. All of my fixtures are worker scoped and have separate timeouts, but it makes no difference to the reported duration of the first tests run by the worker, which still includes the fixture time.

As I already mentioned I'm hoping that the changes introduced in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/15117 address this. They have been merged into main, but not yet tagged in a release. I haven't had success installing the latest commit locally to test. Evidently my package.json skills are lacking in this department!
